attribution: PPG derived from Nutrition Facts / USDA FoodData Central carbohydrate content via lib/fermentable-math.ts (PPG = 46 x available carbohydrate fraction), except where a standard brewing figure exists (dextrose monohydrate, lactose, maltodextrin). Colour values are typical and vary by producer.

fermentables.name: Table Sugar (Sucrose)
fermentables.description: The reference fermentable — 46 PPG by definition. Fully fermentable, dries the finish, boosts ABV without body.
fermentables.usageNotes: Above ~20% of the grist you risk a thin, cidery beer. Standard for Belgian styles and priming.

fermentables.name: Dextrose (Corn Sugar)
fermentables.description: Glucose monohydrate — the water of crystallisation is why it is 42 PPG rather than 46. The standard priming sugar.
fermentables.usageNotes: Yeast take it first and fastest; completely neutral in flavour.

fermentables.name: Turbinado Sugar
fermentables.description: Partially refined cane sugar with a thin film of molasses left on the crystal. Nearly as fermentable as white sugar with a faint caramel note.

fermentables.name: Demerara Sugar
fermentables.description: Large-crystal raw cane sugar; slightly more molasses character than turbinado.

fermentables.name: Light Brown Sugar
fermentables.description: White sugar with molasses added back. Fully fermentable, contributes caramel colour and flavour.

fermentables.name: Dark Brown Sugar
fermentables.description: Higher molasses content than light brown — pronounced toffee and molasses, and real colour contribution.

fermentables.name: Muscovado Sugar
fermentables.description: Unrefined cane sugar retaining most of its molasses; sticky, intense, strongly flavoured.

fermentables.name: Coconut Palm Sugar (Thai)
fermentables.description: Boiled-down coconut palm flower sap, a staple sweetener across Thailand and Southeast Asia. Mostly sucrose with a small inulin fraction (hence a touch of fibre and slightly under 100% fermentability).
fermentables.flavorNotes: Butterscotch, caramel, faint smoke and nuttiness.
fermentables.usageNotes: Sold as hard discs or soft paste; dissolve in hot wort. Adds an aromatic depth plain sugar cannot.

fermentables.name: Jaggery / Gur
fermentables.description: Unrefined South Asian cane or palm sugar, sold in blocks. Widely used in Indian country liquor and increasingly in craft brewing.

fermentables.name: Piloncillo / Panela
fermentables.description: Unrefined Latin American cane sugar cones; the sugar behind Mexican piloncillo stouts and traditional aguardiente.

fermentables.name: Belgian Candi Sugar (Clear)
fermentables.description: Crystallised sucrose used to boost gravity in Belgian tripels and golden strongs without adding body.

fermentables.name: Belgian Candi Syrup D-180
fermentables.description: Deeply caramelised Belgian syrup contributing dark fruit and burnt-sugar complexity to dubbels and quads.

fermentables.name: Molasses
fermentables.description: Cane refining by-product; the base of virtually all rum. Assertive and unmistakable in beer.

fermentables.name: Blackstrap Molasses
fermentables.description: The final, most concentrated molasses extraction — bitter, salty, intensely mineral. A tiny addition dominates.

fermentables.name: Honey
fermentables.description: About 17% water, the rest almost entirely fructose and glucose. The sole fermentable in mead; a delicate addition in beer.
fermentables.usageNotes: Add post-boil or at flame-out — boiling drives off the aromatics you paid for. Varietal matters enormously (orange blossom, buckwheat, clover).
fermentables.flavorNotes: Floral to dark and malty depending on varietal.

fermentables.name: Maple Syrup
fermentables.description: Roughly one-third water. Ferments nearly dry, and most of the maple aroma goes with it — add late and expect subtlety.
fermentables.usageNotes: For actual maple flavour, add at packaging or use a darker Grade B/dark syrup.

fermentables.name: Agave Nectar
fermentables.description: Mostly fructose, so it ferments very dry. Related to (but not the same as) the cooked agave used for tequila and mezcal.

fermentables.name: Sorghum Syrup
fermentables.description: Pressed and boiled sorghum cane juice — a Southern US staple, and a gluten-free gravity source.

fermentables.name: Golden Syrup / Treacle
fermentables.description: Partially inverted cane syrup; a traditional English brewing sugar for milds and old ales.

fermentables.name: Date Syrup
fermentables.description: Boiled date extract used across the Middle East; rich dried-fruit sweetness suited to dark strong ales.

fermentables.name: Lactose (Milk Sugar)
fermentables.description: Brewing yeast cannot ferment lactose at all — it stays in the beer as residual sweetness and body. The defining ingredient of milk stouts and modern pastry/milkshake styles.
fermentables.usageNotes: 0% fermentable: it raises OG and FG equally and does not add alcohol. Not vegan; and note that Saccharomyces cannot touch it but Kluyveromyces marxianus can.

fermentables.name: Maltodextrin
fermentables.description: Unfermentable glucose polymer added purely for body and mouthfeel; flavourless and non-sweet.

fermentables.name: Invert Sugar No. 3
fermentables.description: Graded British invert syrup (No.1 pale through No.4 dark); No.3 brings rich caramel and dried fruit to old ales and porters.

fermentables.name: Dry Malt Extract (Light)
fermentables.description: Dehydrated wort. The standard base for extract brewing and for yeast starters (~100 g per litre gives ~1.040).

Each PDF was fetched and confirmed before being written.

fermentables.name: Liquid Malt Extract (Light)
fermentables.description: Syrup-form malt extract — about 20% water, hence lower PPG than DME.
